split_flag.description: Cheer package names in mock-data.json/MTD carry a 'NO SPLIT' / 'SPLIT' / 'TBD' suffix (e.g. 'PLATINUM 2:30 NO SPLIT'). Cross-checked against every priced package in mtdRecords: the price is identical across all three suffix variants of the same tier+time (e.g. GOLD 1:45 NO SPLIT / SPLIT / TBD are all $700). This confirms the split flag is a delivery-format attribute (whether the routine is mixed/delivered as one continuous file or split into sections) and is PRICE-NEUTRAL. The pricing engine should store it as metadata on the order, not as a pricing input.

voiceovers.description: Recurring miscellaneous voiceover charges from the client's payroll email. Distinct from the per-subtype 'Traditional VOs' / 'Themed VOs' catalog line items already embedded in the pom/hip-hop/team-performance-variety/gameday/jazz-kick subtypes above -- those are fixed-price items tied to a specific subtype; the items below are the general recurring dropdown options and apply wherever a voiceover charge is selected.

dance_voiceover.note: Email: 'Dance Voiceovers - can be $25, $75, or $100.' The $25/$75 tiers match the Traditional VOs / Themed VOs line items already in the dance subtypes; the $100 tier has no definition anywhere -- flagged in Assumptions.

cheer_voiceover.note: Email: 'Cheer Voiceovers - can be $20 or $40.' No cheer voiceover line item exists in any cheer rate-card tab or in mock-data.json -- defined only by the email.

rush_fee.note: Email: 'Rush fee option? $150' and 'Double rush fee - $300.' No triggering rule (turnaround threshold) defined anywhere; not present in mock-data.json today.

eight_count_sheets.note: Email: '8 count sheets. $50.00.' Matches the 'Processing 8ct sheets' line item already priced at $50 inside the youth-rec-cheer subtype. Mock-data.json already has a related but DIFFERENT field: mtdRecords[].eightCountSheet, which is a status string ('HAVE CS' / 'NEED CS' / 'NEED CS & VIDEO' / 'NEED ORDER FORM, CS, & VIDEO'), not a billable line item. Do not confuse the two -- the status field just tracks whether the counts sheet has been received; the $50 addon here is a separate billable service for SLT to produce that sheet.

extra_song.note: Email: 'Extra song - $15 ... quantity ... 3 extra songs; another may need 5.' Total = unit_amount x quantity.

extra_song_added_time_fee.note: Email: 'Extra song added time spent fee - $30 ... quantity.' Total = unit_amount x quantity. Whether this stacks with extra_song per song or is an alternative billing path is unconfirmed (see Assumptions).

existing_mock_data_fields.orders[].musicAffiliate: Already exists in mock-data.json (e.g. 'Power Music Covers'), but is populated on only 2 of 39 sample orders -- the other 37 are null. This is the correct field to drive compliance; it just needs to be populated consistently going forward.
existing_mock_data_fields.mtdRecords[].priceCompliance: Already exists in mock-data.json as 'compliant' / 'non-compliant' -- this is exactly the COMPLIANT/NON-COMPLIANT status the Mark-as-Completed modal needs to show. However, 196 of 197 sample mtdRecords are hardcoded 'compliant' (only one 'non-compliant' row exists), so the sample data can't meaningfully exercise the non-compliant path yet.

compliance_rules.value_normalization_needed: orders[].musicAffiliate uses the value 'Power Music Covers', which does not exactly string-match the rate-card's affiliate list ('Power Music', 'Power Music + Unleash the Beats', 'Unleash the Beats', 'Library Music'). The engine needs a normalization/synonym table (e.g. 'Power Music Covers' -> 'Power Music') rather than a strict equality check, or the order-form's affiliate dropdown needs to be constrained to the exact 4 rate-card values. Flagged in Assumptions.
compliance_rules.compliant_rule: If order.musicAffiliate normalizes to a value in compliant_affiliates AND the package is compliance_sensitive == true, use package.payroll_base_price.compliant, and set priceCompliance = 'compliant'.
compliance_rules.non_compliant_rule: Otherwise, use package.payroll_base_price.non_compliant, and set priceCompliance = 'non-compliant'.
compliance_rules.non_sensitive_rule: If compliance_sensitive == false (Titanium tiers, Fight Song/Alma Mater, School Anthems, JAZZ SIMPLE CUT, most flat VO/addon line items), the compliant and non-compliant payroll-base amounts are equal by design, but priceCompliance should still be computed and shown for transparency.
compliance_rules.unresolved_affiliate_rule: If musicAffiliate is missing/blank/unrecognized (currently true for 37 of 39 sample orders), the engine must flag the order for manual review rather than silently defaulting to either value.

calculation_formulas.payroll_base_price: compliant ? package.payroll_base_price.compliant : package.payroll_base_price.non_compliant, plus addons' own amounts (addons are not compliance-sensitive)
calculation_formulas.final_customer_price: system_calculated_customer_price, unless megan_override is set, in which case final_customer_price = megan_override (system_calculated_customer_price is retained separately for audit)
calculation_formulas.producer_payout: payroll_base_price * producer_rate (or a manual dollar entry for hourly/manual/reimbursement fields)

mock_data_reconciliation_notes.mtdRecords_price_field: Cross-checking every mtdRecords[] row against the rate card shows the existing `price` field is overwhelmingly storing the COMPLIANT PAYROLL-BASE amount, not the customer-facing price (e.g. every 'GOLD 1:30' row is priced at $600 -- the rate card's compliant/payroll amount -- never $700, the actual customer price). This is precisely the conflation the client's task asked us to eliminate, and it's now demonstrated with real data, not just theory.
mock_data_reconciliation_notes.dance_marching_band_sports_anthem_sample: The sample rows for Marching Band, Sports Entertainment, School Anthem, and most Dance subtypes (Gameday, Jazz/Kick) use package names and prices that do not correspond to anything in the rate-card workbook (e.g. a Marching Band order priced with a Cheer-style package name 'GOLD 2:00' at $450; a Gameday order at $425 when the real Gameday rate card tops out at $200). These look like generic placeholder data rather than real historical orders, and will need to be replaced with representative, rate-card-accurate rows to actually demonstrate the pricing engine.
mock_data_reconciliation_notes.discount_codes_undefined: discountCodes[] exists (4 codes) but carries no percentage/amount value anywhere -- if discounts are meant to affect pricing, that rule doesn't exist yet in any source document and is out of scope until defined.
